\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অস্ত্র} (ôstrô)}{অস্ত্র (ôstrô)}]{\bn{অস্ত্র} (ôstrô) — a weapon}

\label{lesson:BN-C315-ostro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a raid, then the Bengali for to occupy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অস্ত্র}}
\textbf{\bn{অস্ত্র}} — \emph{ôstrô} — \textquotedblleft{}a weapon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সৈন্যদের} \bn{হাতে} \bn{অনেক} \bn{অস্ত্র} \bn{ছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{soinyôder hāte ônek ôstrô chhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The soldiers carried many weapons.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অস্ত্র}} (\emph{ôstrô}) is Sanskrit \emph{astra}, a missile weapon, an arrow, and then any weapon (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôstrô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôstrô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{soinyôder hāte ônek ôstrô chhilô.} — The soldiers carried many weapons.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a raid, then the Bengali for to occupy, then say \emph{ôstrô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অস্ত্র} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A weapon\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{তলোয়ার} (tôloyār)}{তলোয়ার (tôloyār)}]{\bn{তলোয়ার} (tôloyār) — a sword}

\label{lesson:BN-C315-toloyar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to occupy, then the Bengali for a weapon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{তলোয়ার}}
\textbf{\bn{তলোয়ার}} — \emph{tôloyār} — \textquotedblleft{}a sword\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাজকুমার} \bn{তলোয়ার} \bn{নিয়ে} \bn{শত্রুর} \bn{সঙ্গে} \bn{লড়লেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rājkumār tôloyār niye shôtrur sôngge lôṛlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The prince took up his sword and fought the enemy.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{তলোয়ার}} (\emph{tôloyār}) is usually traced to Sanskrit \emph{taravāri}, 'a one-edged sword' (CDIAL 5706; Monier-Williams), which Monier-Williams wonders may stand for \emph{tala-v-}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tôloyār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tôloyār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rājkumār tôloyār niye shôtrur sôngge lôṛlen.} — The prince took up his sword and fought the enemy.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to occupy, then the Bengali for a weapon, then say \emph{tôloyār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{তলোয়ার} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A sword\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ঢাল} (ḍhāl)}{ঢাল (ḍhāl)}]{\bn{ঢাল} (ḍhāl) — a shield}

\label{lesson:BN-C315-dhal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a weapon, then the Bengali for a sword.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ঢাল}}
\textbf{\bn{ঢাল}} — \emph{ḍhāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a shield\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সৈন্যরা} \bn{ঢাল} \bn{আর} \bn{তলোয়ার} \bn{নিয়ে} \bn{এগোল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{soinyôrā ḍhāl ār tôloyār niye egolô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The soldiers advanced with shields and swords.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ঢাল}} (\emph{ḍhāl}) comes down from Sanskrit \emph{ḍhāla}, 'a shield' (CDIAL 5583, which lists Bengali \emph{ḍhāl}). Another \bn{ঢাল}, a slope, is a different word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍhāl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍhāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{soinyôrā ḍhāl ār tôloyār niye egolô.} — The soldiers advanced with shields and swords.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a weapon, then the Bengali for a sword, then say \emph{ḍhāl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ঢাল} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A shield\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বন্দুক} (bônduk)}{বন্দুক (bônduk)}]{\bn{বন্দুক} (bônduk) — a gun}

\label{lesson:BN-C315-bonduk}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a sword, then the Bengali for a shield.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বন্দুক}}
\textbf{\bn{বন্দুক}} — \emph{bônduk} — \textquotedblleft{}a gun\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পুলিশের} \bn{হাতে} \bn{বন্দুক} \bn{ছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pulisher hāte bônduk chhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police were carrying guns.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বন্দুক}} (\emph{bônduk}) is usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{bunduq}, a hazelnut and then a pellet; the name passed from the shot to the gun.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bônduk}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bônduk}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pulisher hāte bônduk chhilô.} — The police were carrying guns.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a sword, then the Bengali for a shield, then say \emph{bônduk} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বন্দুক} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A gun\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কামান} (kāmān)}{কামান (kāmān)}]{\bn{কামান} (kāmān) — a cannon}

\label{lesson:BN-C315-kaman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a shield, then the Bengali for a gun.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কামান}}
\textbf{\bn{কামান}} — \emph{kāmān} — \textquotedblleft{}a cannon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দুর্গের} \bn{ছাদে} \bn{একটা} \bn{পুরনো} \bn{কামান} \bn{আছে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{durger chhāde ekṭā purôno kāmān āchhe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is an old cannon on the roof of the fort.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কামান}} (\emph{kāmān}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{kamān}, 'a bow'; the name passed from the bow to the gun.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāmān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāmān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durger chhāde ekṭā purôno kāmān āchhe.} — There is an old cannon on the roof of the fort.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a shield, then the Bengali for a gun, then say \emph{kāmān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{কামান} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cannon\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from The Last Day of the Festival to Swords and Cannons}

\label{lesson:BN-R315-review-308-315}



\begin{quote}
Say the Bengali for the immersion of an idol and to set afloat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the immersion of an idol, to set afloat, a farewell, a festive procession, to embrace
  \item a paper kite, to fly a kite, the new year, a new account book, a custom
  \item a conch shell, to pray, a devotee, a goddess, holy
  \item a Ferris wheel, a puppet show, a balloon, to go round, packed
  \item a ceremony, a garland, a shehnai, ululation, the groom's wedding party
  \item a kingdom, an emperor, a throne, a crown, to rule
  \item an enemy, a soldier, to attack, a raid, to occupy
  \item a weapon, a sword, a shield, a gun, a cannon
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The immersion of an idol? (\textbf{\bn{বিসর্জন}}, \emph{bisôrjôn}.) To set afloat? (\textbf{\bn{ভাসানো}}, \emph{bhāsāno}.) A farewell? (\textbf{\bn{বিদায়}}, \emph{bidāy}.) A festive procession? (\textbf{\bn{শোভাযাত্রা}}, \emph{shobhājātrā}.) To embrace? (\textbf{\bn{কোলাকুলি} \bn{করা}}, \emph{kolākuli kôrā}.) A paper kite? (\textbf{\bn{ঘুড়ি}}, \emph{ghuṛi}.) To fly a kite? (\textbf{\bn{ওড়ানো}}, \emph{oṛāno}.) The new year? (\textbf{\bn{নববর্ষ}}, \emph{nôbôbôrshô}.) A new account book? (\textbf{\bn{হালখাতা}}, \emph{hālkhātā}.) A custom? (\textbf{\bn{প্রথা}}, \emph{prôthā}.) A conch shell? (\textbf{\bn{শঙ্খ}}, \emph{shôngkhô}.) To pray? (\textbf{\bn{প্রার্থনা} \bn{করা}}, \emph{prārthônā kôrā}.) A devotee? (\textbf{\bn{ভক্ত}}, \emph{bhôktô}.) A goddess? (\textbf{\bn{দেবী}}, \emph{debī}.) Holy? (\textbf{\bn{পবিত্র}}, \emph{pôbitrô}.) A Ferris wheel? (\textbf{\bn{নাগরদোলা}}, \emph{nāgôrdolā}.) A puppet show? (\textbf{\bn{পুতুলনাচ}}, \emph{putulnāch}.) A balloon? (\textbf{\bn{বেলুন}}, \emph{belun}.) To go round? (\textbf{\bn{ঘোরা}}, \emph{ghorā}.) Packed? (\textbf{\bn{ঠাসা}}, \emph{ṭhāsā}.) A ceremony? (\textbf{\bn{অনুষ্ঠান}}, \emph{ônushṭhān}.) A garland? (\textbf{\bn{মালা}}, \emph{mālā}.) A shehnai? (\textbf{\bn{সানাই}}, \emph{sānāi}.) Ululation? (\textbf{\bn{উলু}}, \emph{ulu}.) The groom's wedding party? (\textbf{\bn{বরযাত্রী}}, \emph{bôrjātrī}.) A kingdom? (\textbf{\bn{রাজ্য}}, \emph{rājyô}.) An emperor? (\textbf{\bn{সম্রাট}}, \emph{sômrāṭ}.) A throne? (\textbf{\bn{সিংহাসন}}, \emph{singhāsôn}.) A crown? (\textbf{\bn{মুকুট}}, \emph{mukuṭ}.) To rule? (\textbf{\bn{শাসন} \bn{করা}}, \emph{shāsôn kôrā}.) An enemy? (\textbf{\bn{শত্রু}}, \emph{shôtru}.) A soldier? (\textbf{\bn{সৈন্য}}, \emph{soinyô}.) To attack? (\textbf{\bn{আক্রমণ} \bn{করা}}, \emph{ākrômôn kôrā}.) A raid? (\textbf{\bn{হামলা}}, \emph{hāmlā}.) To occupy? (\textbf{\bn{দখল} \bn{করা}}, \emph{dôkhôl kôrā}.) A weapon? (\textbf{\bn{অস্ত্র}}, \emph{ôstrô}.) A sword? (\textbf{\bn{তলোয়ার}}, \emph{tôloyār}.) A shield? (\textbf{\bn{ঢাল}}, \emph{ḍhāl}.) A gun? (\textbf{\bn{বন্দুক}}, \emph{bônduk}.) A cannon? (\textbf{\bn{কামান}}, \emph{kāmān}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
